question: A nurse needs to weigh a patient wearing a heavy leg cast that cannot be taken off. How should this be documented?

options.A: Guess how much the cast weighs and subtract that amount from the scale reading
options.B: Record the weight and add a clear note stating the patient was wearing a leg cast
options.C: Omit the weight entry entirely from the patient chart until the cast comes off
options.D: Record the weight without any mention of the cast so the chart looks normal

explanation: Always document the facts! Adding a note about the cast helps other nurses understand why the weight is higher without guessing. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T3#GNS112_U6_T3_h8)

question: Why must chest compressions pause briefly when someone is giving an intracardiac injection?

options.A: To ensure the intravenous line stays securely in place
options.B: To prevent the needle from moving and tearing the heart muscle
options.C: To keep the patient from waking up during the procedure
options.D: To allow the nurse time to chart the medication administration

explanation: Safety first! CPR makes the chest bounce around, which would cause a needle inside the heart to rip the muscle tissue. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T14#GNS125_U3_T14_h5)

question: A patient comes to the clinic with severe lower belly pain and irregular bleeding. What is the best first nursing action?

options.A: Take a detailed menstrual history, including her last period date
options.B: Prepare her for immediate surgery
options.C: Tell the patient menopause has started
options.D: Advise her to stop all physical activity

explanation: Brilliant! Always start with a thorough history. Knowing her menstrual pattern helps the team figure out what might be going wrong. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T2#GNS311_U1_T2_h7)

question: A patient gets a painkiller derived from the opium poppy after surgery. Which drug is it?

options.A: Quinine
options.B: Atropine
options.C: Morphine
options.D: Digoxin

explanation: Morphine is a powerful pain-relieving medication extracted right from the opium poppy plant. You'll see this often in clinicals! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T3#GNS125_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why do nurses calculate a patient's BMI during clinical assessments?

options.A: To screen for potential weight-related health risks
options.B: To determine exact daily caloric requirements
options.C: To diagnose specific cardiovascular diseases
options.D: To directly measure total body fat percentage

explanation: Great job! BMI is a quick, handy screening tool to flag weight categories that might put a patient at health risk, even though it doesn't measure fat directly. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T10#GNS121_U1_T10_h1)

question: Ten minutes after delivery, a mum starts bleeding heavily and her uterus feels soft and boggy. What should you do right away?

options.A: Encourage the mother to walk around the room to boost circulation
options.B: Wait patiently for thirty minutes to see if the bleeding stops on its own
options.C: Send the patient home immediately with iron tablets
options.D: Perform fundal massage and administer the prescribed uterotonic drug

explanation: Well done! Massaging the uterus helps it contract, and giving the uterotonic medication stops the bleeding fast. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T15#GNS324_U5_T15_h6)

question: What is the main job of a patient referral form in community health?

options.A: To replace the patient's daily hospital bed ticket
options.B: To serve as a permanent financial receipt for clinic services
options.C: To connect a patient with higher levels of specialized care
options.D: To discharge a patient permanently from all medical follow-up

explanation: You've got this! Referral forms act like a bridge, safely moving a patient from our basic community clinics up to advanced centers when they need extra specialist attention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h1)

question: What special addition is often necessary when a patient is placed on a very strict low protein diet?

options.A: High-sodium tablets to maintain blood pressure
options.B: Essential amino acid or keto acid supplements
options.C: Concentrated liquid sugar for quick energy
options.D: Extra doses of water-soluble vitamins only

explanation: Strict restriction removes too many vital building blocks, so medical supplements are added to prevent the body from breaking down its own muscle tissue. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T004#GNS227_U6_T004_h3)

question: Which everyday substance must definitely be kept out of a stool sample?

options.A: Normal saline
options.B: Tap water
options.C: Paper towels
options.D: Urine

explanation: Urine mixes easily with stool and can ruin lab tests for parasites or blood. Always ask patients to pass urine first! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T4#GNS112_U6_T4_h4)

question: What usually happens if a patient accidentally swallows a sublingual tablet with water?

options.A: The drug will turn into a toxic substance in the intestines.
options.B: The drug may be destroyed by stomach acid and liver enzymes.
options.C: There will be no change in how the drug works.
options.D: The drug will absorb twice as fast through the stomach lining.

explanation: Correct! Swallowing it means it faces stomach acid and the liver, which can weaken or destroy the drug before it works. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h5)

question: Which of these structures sits right inside the vaginal vestibule?

options.A: Fallopian tube ampulla
options.B: Uterine fundus
options.C: Ovarian follicle
options.D: External urethral opening

explanation: Well done! The vestibule is the space where both the opening for urine (urethra) and the vagina are located. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T3#GNS121_U5_T3_h5)

question: Why do researchers need to narrow down a massive topic like 'hospital stress'?

options.A: Broad topics are too massive and vague to study effectively all at once
options.B: Patients refuse to talk about general topics
options.C: Narrowing a topic increases the financial cost of the study
options.D: Broad topics are illegal to research in clinical settings

explanation: If your topic is as big as the ocean, you'll drown in data! Narrowing it down gives you a specific pool you can easily swim across. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T2#GNS217_U3_T2_h7)

question: Which lung issue is most common for a patient stuck on prolonged bed rest in traction?

options.A: Hyperventilation syndrome
options.B: Asthma attack
options.C: Atelectasis
options.D: Spontaneous pneumothorax

explanation: Well done! Lying flat and breathing shallowly can cause small air sacs in the lungs to collapse (atelectasis). That's why deep breathing exercises and incentive spirometry are so important! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T9#GNS221_U1_T9_h5)

question: A patient taking ethambutol reports noticing a change in their vision. What should you do first?

options.A: Report the visual changes promptly to the prescriber.
options.B: Double the next dose of the medication.
options.C: Advise the patient to stop eating green vegetables.
options.D: Reassure the patient that blurry vision is a normal temporary sign.

explanation: Ethambutol can affect the eyes (optic neuritis). Any vision changes need a quick report to the doctor so we can protect the patient's sight! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T5#GNS214_U1_T5_h8)

question: Why do pelvic organ prolapse conditions often lead to problems with urination?

options.A: Estrogen surges cause the bladder to double in physical size
options.B: Infection destroys the smooth muscle tissue of the ureters
options.C: The kidneys stop producing urine due to chronic pelvic pressure
options.D: The shifted position of the organs changes normal urine flow mechanics

explanation: When supportive pelvic structures weaken and sag, organs like the bladder shift out of place. This makes it hard to empty the bladder fully, leading to frequent urges or retention. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h3)

question: Which part of our digestive tract is the main site for drug absorption because of its huge surface area?

options.A: Esophagus
options.B: Small intestine
options.C: Stomach lining
options.D: Large colon

explanation: The small intestine is packed with tiny finger-like folds (villi) that create a massive surface area, perfect for absorbing nutrients and drugs! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T1#GNS125_U5_T1_h5)

question: What is the specific name for Cushing's syndrome when it is caused by a tiny tumor in the pituitary gland making too much ACTH?

options.A: Cushing's disease
options.B: Conn's syndrome
options.C: Pheochromocytoma
options.D: Addison's disease

explanation: Here is a handy clinical tip: 'Cushing's syndrome' is any excess cortisol, but when the pituitary gland's tumor is the culprit, we specifically call it 'Cushing's disease'. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T12#GNS222_U2_T12_h4)

question: What is the main difference between a target population and an accessible population?

options.A: The target population is smaller than the accessible population
options.B: The accessible population includes dead patients, but the target population does not
options.C: There is no difference between these two terms in nursing studies
options.D: The target population is the ideal group, while the accessible group can actually be reached

explanation: Great thinking! The target group is your dream group (everyone with the condition), while the accessible group is the realistic bunch right there in your hospital that you can actually talk to and study. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T16#GNS224_U1_T16_h2)

question: A nurse records a patient's exact weight in kilograms. What type of measurement scale is this?

options.A: Nominal scale
options.B: Interval scale
options.C: Ordinal scale
options.D: Ratio scale

explanation: Weight is measured on a ratio scale because it has equal intervals and a true zero point where zero kilograms means an absolute absence of weight. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h2)

question: Why is it so crucial to ask a patient about their past medical history?

options.A: It reveals chronic conditions that affect current symptoms
options.B: It tells you what the patient eats for breakfast
options.C: It replaces the need to ask about the present illness
options.D: It proves whether the patient takes their medication daily

explanation: Exactly! Knowing past health issues helps you understand how older illnesses might be mixing with or causing today's trouble. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T1#GNS124_U6_T1_h5)

question: Where is the body's center of gravity usually located when standing normally?

options.A: Inside the left ventricle
options.B: In the center of the pelvis
options.C: At the top of the skull
options.D: Directly between both feet

explanation: When standing straight, our center of balance or gravity is right around our pelvic area. Knowing this helps us understand how our bodies stay stable! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h2)

question: Where does the fluid from the lymph vessels in the external genitalia primarily drain?

options.A: Deep pelvic lymph nodes only
options.B: Aortic and renal lymph nodes
options.C: Axillary lymph nodes in the chest
options.D: Superficial inguinal lymph nodes

explanation: Spot on! Lymph from the vulva drains mainly to the superficial nodes right there in the groin (inguinal) area. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T1#GNS121_U5_T1_h7)

question: Where do the nerve fibers in the dorsal column pathway cross over to the opposite side of the body?

options.A: The lumbar spinal cord
options.B: The peripheral skin receptor
options.C: The medulla oblongata
options.D: The cerebral cortex

explanation: Spot on! As these sensory messages travel up, they cross over to the other side once they reach the lower part of the brainstem called the medulla. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T11#GNS211_U4_T11_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse checks for safety during a first home visit?

options.A: Safety and cleanliness of the water supply
options.B: Presence of loose rugs or cluttered walkways
options.C: Condition of electrical wiring and cooking areas
options.D: Availability of high-tech robotic surgery equipment

explanation: Correct! We don't expect high-tech operating theatre equipment in a house. Our focus is purely on everyday home safety hazards. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T5#GNS324_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the main goal of the science of improvement in healthcare?

options.A: Reducing hospital operational costs by cutting nursing staff numbers
options.B: Punishing staff members who make medication administration errors
options.C: Discovering entirely new medical treatments through laboratory trials
options.D: Applying proven knowledge to reliably improve daily care processes

explanation: Improvement science simply means taking what we already know works and finding practical, everyday ways to use it consistently in the ward. You've got this! [learn more](GST319_U2_T2#GST319_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which nursing action helps a hospitalized patient cough up thick mucus more easily?

options.A: Encouraging fluids and deep breathing exercises
options.B: Keeping the patient lying flat in bed all day
options.C: Restricting water to prevent fluid buildup in the lungs
options.D: Giving strong sleeping pills to stop the cough

explanation: Water is a natural thinner for mucus! Combined with deep breathing and controlled coughing, it helps clear the airways safely. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T6#GNS213_U2_T6_h7)

question: What is the main difference between primary and secondary skin lesions?

options.A: Primary lesions require surgical removal, while secondary lesions always resolve without any intervention
options.B: Primary lesions only appear on the face, while secondary lesions are found exclusively on the lower extremities
options.C: Primary lesions are always painless, whereas secondary lesions always cause severe systemic fever
options.D: Primary lesions develop directly from the disease process, while secondary ones result from changes like scratching or healing

explanation: You got it! Primary lesions pop up straight from the illness itself, while secondary ones form later due to things like scratching or scabbing. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T6#GNS213_U5_T6_h3)

question: A patient needs an IV that won't get blocked every time they bend their arm. Which spot should you avoid?

options.A: The dorsal metacarpal network
options.B: The antecubital fossa
options.C: The back of the hand
options.D: The lower forearm veins

explanation: The antecubital fossa sits right at the inner elbow crease. When the patient bends their arm, the tubing kinks and the pump starts beeping. Better to pick a spot on the forearm or hand! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T5#GNS125_U3_T5_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a common reason why nurses resist clinical change?

options.A: Excitement about learning too many new computer systems at once
options.B: Skepticism because past projects failed
options.C: Fear of a heavier workload during busy shifts
options.D: Comfort with familiar, everyday routines

explanation: Well done! Nurses rarely resist change because they are 'too excited' about computers. Resistance usually comes from pure fatigue, fear, and burnout. [learn more](GST319_U1_T4#GST319_U1_T4_h5)

question: What molecule builds up inside muscle cells to help them relax when a beta-2 agonist is used?

options.A: Cyclic AMP (cAMP)
options.B: Acetylcholine
options.C: Calcium ions
options.D: Phosphodiesterase

explanation: When beta-2 agonists do their magic, they boost cAMP levels inside the cell, which tells the muscle to relax and let go of the tightness. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T2#GNS223_U2_T2_h3)

question: What kind of data do you collect when you count clinic attendance numbers and disease tallies?

options.A: Quantitative data
options.B: Fictional data
options.C: Qualitative data
options.D: Financial data

explanation: Whenever you see numbers and amounts (like tally counts), remember that's quantitative data! [learn more](GNS124_U3_T8#GNS124_U3_T8_h3)

question: Why should approved drug prices be clearly posted on notice boards near hospital pharmacies?

options.A: To advertise the hospital services to private pharmaceutical competitors
options.B: To comply with international tax collection laws
options.C: To encourage patients to donate money to the pharmacy
options.D: To ensure transparency and prevent staff from overcharging patients

explanation: Transparency is key! Displaying official prices openly protects vulnerable patients from exploitation and keeps everyone honest. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T5#GNS215_U3_T5_h7)

question: What does the skin usually look like right after a long-term cast is removed?

options.A: Bright red, inflamed, and completely covered in blisters
options.B: Dry, scaly, and pale with accumulated dead skin cells
options.C: Deeply tanned from being shielded from outdoor sunlight
options.D: Oily, moist, and smelling strongly of fresh antiseptic lotion

explanation: Because dead skin cells couldn't shed normally while trapped in the cast, the skin looks dry and flaky when the cast finally comes off. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h8)

question: Which airway maneuver should you use if you think your patient has a neck or spine injury?

options.A: Jaw-thrust maneuver
options.B: Lateral neck rotation
options.C: Rapid neck hyperextension
options.D: Head-tilt, chin-lift maneuver

explanation: The jaw-thrust opens the airway without bending or moving the neck, keeping the cervical spine safe from further harm. Brilliant nursing judgment! [learn more](GNS221_U3_T6#GNS221_U3_T6_h6)

question: Which of these is a bad practice when looking at clinical data?

options.A: Looking at trends over several months instead of one week
options.B: Ignoring the denominator when looking at small sample sizes
options.C: Reviewing how patient data was collected in the first place
options.D: Checking whether two events are truly related before acting

explanation: Well done! Forgetting the total number of patients can make a tiny issue look like a massive epidemic. Always check the whole picture! [learn more](GST319_U1_T2#GST319_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which substances were historically harvested directly from animals for medical use?

options.A: Petroleum-based solvents
options.B: Pure mineral salts and water
options.C: Synthetic plastics and nylon
options.D: Hormones and insulin

explanation: Before lab technology advanced, we relied heavily on animal organs—like pig and cow pancreases—to get insulin for diabetic patients. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T5#GNS125_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which type of sleep is mostly connected to dreaming and sorting out memories?

options.A: Rapid eye movement sleep
options.B: Stage one non-rapid eye movement sleep
options.C: Deep metabolic resting phase
options.D: Conscious alpha wave waking state

explanation: REM (Rapid Eye Movement) sleep is that active brain phase where vivid dreams happen and your mind processes everything you learned during the day. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T1#GNS223_U6_T1_h2)

question: What is eutrophication in plain terms?

options.A: A sudden increase of clean mineral nutrients in underground wells
options.B: The natural warming of river water by industrial thermal plants
options.C: Oxygen depletion in water caused by the decomposition of excess algae
options.D: The direct filtration of heavy metals through sandy soil layers

explanation: You got it! Too many nutrients cause massive algae blooms; when those plants die and rot, they suck all the oxygen out of the water. [learn more](GST114_U6_T6#GST114_U6_T6_h5)

question: Which hormones flood the body during a 'fight or flight' response when a mum is distressed?

options.A: Adrenaline and noradrenaline
options.B: Estrogen and progesterone
options.C: Thyroid stimulating hormones
options.D: Insulin and glucagon

explanation: When fear or severe stress hits, the nervous system kicks into gear and releases catecholamines like adrenaline and noradrenaline. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T002#GNS226_U4_T002_h2)

question: What is the main functional difference between the front (anterior) and back (posterior) lobes of the pituitary gland?

options.A: The anterior lobe responds to nervous signals, while the posterior lobe responds exclusively to chemical blood signals
options.B: The anterior lobe synthesizes its own hormones, while the posterior lobe only stores and releases them
options.C: The posterior lobe produces releasing factors, while the anterior lobe targets the hypothalamus
options.D: The posterior lobe contains glandular epithelial cords, while the anterior lobe is made entirely of neurons

explanation: Remember: the anterior pituitary is a factory that makes its own hormones, while the posterior pituitary is more like a warehouse that just stores and sends out what the brain (hypothalamus) made for it! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a main focus during external regulatory inspections of a nursing home?

options.A: Checking employee vacation requests and holiday schedules
options.B: Evaluating medication administration accuracy and safety
options.C: Ensuring residents' rights and personal dignity are protected
options.D: Assessing environmental safety and infection control practices

explanation: You got this! Inspectors care about resident safety, care quality, and rights—they don't mind who takes holiday when! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T9#GNS324_U5_T9_h6)

question: Which lymphoid organ is primarily responsible for filtering blood and destroying old red blood cells?

options.A: Spleen
options.B: Thymus
options.C: Liver
options.D: Tonsil

explanation: The spleen filters blood, recycles iron from hemoglobin, and removes damaged red blood cells. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h4)

question: What is the very first thing an infection control team does when investigating a possible outbreak?

options.A: Fire the nursing supervisor in charge of the affected ward
options.B: Immediately shut down the entire hospital and send all patients home
options.C: Verify the diagnoses and clearly define what counts as a case
options.D: Hold a press conference to warn the public about the danger

explanation: Spot on! Before hunting for the source, you first need to be sure real infections are happening and set clear rules for what you are counting. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h6)

question: A nurse is caring for a patient recovering from major surgery. Who is the best healthcare professional to consult for a custom diet plan?

options.A: Physical therapist
options.B: Biomedical technician
options.C: Registered dietitian
options.D: Hospital pharmacist

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Dietitians are the absolute experts at calculating precise calories and nutrients for patients who need special nutritional healing. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h7)

question: How many weeks of pregnancy make up a normal term delivery?

options.A: 37 to 42 weeks
options.B: 40 to 45 weeks
options.C: 30 to 35 weeks
options.D: 24 to 28 weeks

explanation: Great job! A normal, healthy pregnancy usually lasts between 37 and 42 weeks before natural labour begins. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h1)

question: Which simple home practice helps cut down the spread of airborne TB?

options.A: Keeping the patient bedroom door tightly locked at all times
options.B: Using chemical disinfectants to wipe down furniture daily
options.C: Washing all patient eating utensils in boiling water
options.D: Opening windows frequently to ensure good room ventilation

explanation: Fresh air is a powerful ally! Opening windows blows away and dilutes airborne TB germs so others don't breathe them in. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T18#GNS324_U4_T18_h6)

question: What should an instructor do if students keep struggling to understand a concept after a lesson?

options.A: Blame the students for lacking basic intelligence
options.B: Ignore the failure and move on to the next chapter
options.C: Remove all practical work from the nursing curriculum
options.D: Revise the activity or adjust the teaching method

explanation: If a topic is tough to grasp, a good educator changes the approach so everyone can succeed. Learning is a two-way street! [learn more](GST321_U8_T5#GST321_U8_T5_h6)

question: Why is it recommended to start a PDSA test with just one patient or one nurse?

options.A: Patients refuse to let more than one nurse care for them
options.B: It guarantees that no data will ever need to be collected
options.C: It minimizes risk and makes it easy to adjust the idea if something goes wrong
options.D: Hospital regulations forbid testing on more than one person at a time

explanation: Great thinking! Starting microscopically small keeps patients safe and prevents staff burnout while you work out the kinks. [learn more](GST319_U2_T8#GST319_U2_T8_h7)

question: Which cranial nerve is mainly responsible for controlling the muscles of the oesophagus?

options.A: Glossopharyngeal nerve
options.B: Hypoglossal nerve
options.C: Trigeminal nerve
options.D: Vagus nerve

explanation: Correct! The vagus nerve is the major highway for signals that coordinate those smooth swallowing contractions. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T2#GNS121_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why is complete chest recoil important between individual chest compressions?

options.A: It keeps the patient's lungs inflated with fresh air
options.B: It gives the rescuer's tired arm muscles a chance to rest
options.C: It prevents the ribs from fracturing during compressions
options.D: It lets the heart chambers fill back up with blood

explanation: If the chest does not recoil fully, the heart cannot refill properly, making the next compression useless. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why is a personalized nutrition chat usually better than just handing a patient a printed meal plan?

options.A: It guarantees rapid weight loss without any effort
options.B: It replaces the need for medical checkups entirely
options.C: It costs nothing for the healthcare facility to provide
options.D: It takes into account the patient's personal lifestyle and culture

explanation: Spot on! Generic meal plans often fail because they ignore how people actually live and eat at home. Tailoring your advice to their culture and routine makes all the difference. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T003#GNS227_U7_T003_h1)

question: What should you do right away if your patient feels sharp belly cramps while you are running the fluid?

options.A: Stop the flow immediately until the cramp passes
options.B: Ignore the symptom as a normal expected reaction
options.C: Raise the fluid container higher to finish quickly
options.D: Push the rectal tube deeper into the sigmoid colon

explanation: Cramping means the bowel is filling up too fast! Always pause the flow and let the patient relax before starting again. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h5)

question: How does stomach acid help protect you from getting sick?

options.A: By coating the intestinal lining with a thick mucus
options.B: By destroying ingested bacteria and other microorganisms
options.C: By producing specific antibodies against food antigens
options.D: By stimulating the production of white blood cells

explanation: Exactly! The strong acid in your stomach acts like a harsh chemical bath that kills most of the germs you accidentally swallow with your food or water. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T2#GNS123_U4_T2_h2)

question: What are the two main gonadotropins released by the anterior pituitary gland?

options.A: Cortisol and aldosterone
options.B: Insulin and glucagon
options.C: FSH and LH
options.D: Thyroxine and calcitonin

explanation: Spot on! Follicle-Stimulating Hormone (FSH) and Luteinizing Hormone (LH) are the key team players secreted by the anterior pituitary. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T13#GNS121_U5_T13_h3)

question: How are blood-borne infections like HIV and Hepatitis B mainly spread during traditional FGM?

options.A: Exposure to contaminated air in rural communities
options.B: Drinking contaminated water after the procedure
options.C: Insect bites during outdoor healing rituals
options.D: Reusing unsterilized cutting instruments on multiple individuals

explanation: Spot on! Using the same knife or razor blade for different girls without cleaning it passes blood and infections directly between them. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T4#GNS225_U6_T4_h6)

question: Which electrolyte is found mostly inside the cells and is vital for heart rhythm?

options.A: Potassium
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Sodium
options.D: Chloride

explanation: Potassium is the chief intracellular cation, and even small changes in its level can dangerously disrupt heart rhythm. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T7#GNS123_U3_T7_h3)

question: How do nurses usually record how much of a meal a patient actually ate in the chart?

options.A: Counting every individual grain of rice
options.B: Taking a photo of the tray after eating
options.C: Weighing food scraps on a gram scale
options.D: Percentage estimation of the meal eaten

explanation: That's right! We estimate intake in quarters (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) to quickly track how much nourishment they got. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h5)

question: What shape is an intrauterine device (IUD)?

options.A: T-shaped
options.B: Spiral-shaped
options.C: Capsule-shaped
options.D: Ring-shaped

explanation: IUDs are built with a small frame shaped like the letter T so they fit comfortably inside the uterine cavity. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h1)

question: Which simple test helps find hidden blood in a patient's stool?

options.A: Fast blood glucose test
options.B: Routine urinalysis
options.C: Fecal occult blood test
options.D: Serum electrolyte panel

explanation: The word 'occult' means hidden! This stool test catches tiny traces of blood that your eyes can't see. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T2#GNS213_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why might a nurse researcher choose an observational checklist instead of a patient questionnaire?

options.A: Patients prefer being watched over writing answers
options.B: What people say they do can differ from their actual actions
options.C: Observational checklists are much cheaper to print
options.D: Questionnaires cannot be used in a hospital setting

explanation: Direct observation captures real behavior, avoiding the bias or forgetfulness that comes with self-reporting. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h5)

question: What is motivation mainly about in everyday nursing?

options.A: The financial bonus earned after a successful procedure
options.B: The strict adherence to hospital policies and routines

question: Which of these features is typically seen in a female pelvis rather than a male pelvis?

question: Why is it important for hospital leadership to show staff that audit data leads to real changes?

question: What is the main purpose of an improvement plan on a hospital ward?

question: A glass bottle of lab specimen drops and shatters on the floor, creating a large spill. What should you do first?

question: Why should community midwives collaborate with traditional birth attendants instead of ignoring them?

question: Where does a National Health Insurance Scheme usually get most of its money from?

question: Who are key local figures nurses should partner with to improve community trust during an outbreak?

question: How do contact tracing and patient interviews help during an outbreak?

question: When writing a good research question, which of these is an absolute must?

question: What is the biggest challenge faced by child-headed households?

question: Why do doctors avoid doing a direct needle biopsy of a heart mass?

question: What is the main goal of community nursing advocacy for smoke-free indoor public spaces?

question: Which type of joint is known for having a fluid-filled space between the bones?

question: Opened in 1907, which facility was Nigeria's very first psychiatric institution?

question: Which of the following is NOT a goal of community health education on infections?

question: At what exact moment in your daily clinical routine should you sort and segregate hospital waste?

question: What is the main goal of Directly Observed Therapy (DOT) for TB patients?

options.A: Reducing the overall financial cost of purchasing prescription drugs

question: Which key immune cells are primarily attacked and destroyed by HIV?

question: What happens during a standard knee-jerk reflex test?

question: What is the term for high blood pressure that has no single identifiable medical cause?

question: What happens to the baby's skull bones during moulding in labour?

question: Which of the following is a common misconception about dominant genetic disorders that nurses often correct?

question: A family caregiver feels super guilty just for wanting a single day off. What does this most likely point to?

question: An elderly client with limited mobility spends most of the day lying in bed. What is the most important preventive action the caregiver should take?

question: An emergency patient needs medicine right now. Which route will work the fastest?

question: Why do we make time for psychological support and talking after a traumatic, high-risk birth?

question: Where should the money come from to pay for drugs given out under an exemption policy?

question: Why is economic stability so important when a community health nurse tries to lower disease rates?

question: What does the accessibility principle mean in youth-friendly health services?

question: What is the primary goal of health education?

question: How does poor hospital infrastructure affect a nurse's daily shift?

question: Which of these is NOT a good nursing intervention for supporting a patient's mental health?

question: Why must physical patient registers and folders be locked away in storage cabinets when not in use?

question: Which lifestyle change helps the most in managing stress incontinence?

question: Why might two people taking the exact same dose of cough syrup react completely differently?

question: How does a memory lapse differ from a mistake in everyday nursing practice?

question: What is needed to make community health schemes truly successful in Nigeria?

question: Why must nurse managers be careful with how much time is spent in meetings?

question: In nursing care, what does 'identity reconstruction' mean for someone with a new physical disability?

options.C: Replacing all lost body parts with artificial ones
options.D: Undergoing plastic surgery to hide all physical scars

explanation: Correct! It's all about helping them accept their physical changes and learn to love and value themselves in a new way. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T14#GNS225_U5_T14_h4)

question: A nurse is packing a vaccine carrier for an outreach. What must be avoided to protect the vaccines?

options.A: Keeping the lid of the vaccine carrier tightly closed between uses
options.B: Placing frozen ice packs directly touching liquid vaccines
options.C: Lining the bottom of the vaccine carrier with conditioned ice packs
options.D: Checking the temperature of the cold box using a stem thermometer

explanation: Spot on! Direct contact with freezing ice can ruin liquid vaccines like pentavalent by freezing them solid. Always use conditioned ice packs! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T63#GNS214_U1_T63_h3)

question: Even though a benign tumor is non-cancerous, why can it still be dangerous to a patient?

options.A: It always releases toxic poisons into the bloodstream
options.B: It can press on vital structures inside confined spaces
options.C: It frequently turns into widespread blood cancer
options.D: It destroys the immune system completely

explanation: Think about a crowded room! Even if things are peaceful, if a tumor grows inside a tight space like the skull, it can press on vital organs and cause serious trouble. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T6#GNS321_U1_T6_h2)

question: Which degree of perineal tear affects only the vaginal skin and mucous membrane?

options.A: Third-degree tear
options.B: First-degree tear
options.C: Fourth-degree tear
options.D: Second-degree tear

explanation: A first-degree tear is very minor and superficial, touching only the skin and mucous membranes without getting into the deeper muscles. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h2)

question: What actually happens during a percutaneous transluminal angioplasty procedure?

options.A: An incompetent vein valve is surgically tightened with sutures.
options.B: A balloon-tipped catheter is inflated to compress arterial plaque.
options.C: A chemical medication is injected directly to dissolve fatty deposits.
options.D: A synthetic tube is sewn around a blocked section of an artery.

explanation: During angioplasty, the doctor threads a tiny deflated balloon to the blockage and blows it up like a balloon to squish the plaque flat against the artery wall. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T5#GNS123_U5_T5_h6)

question: Who was one of the very first industrial visiting nurses in the US, starting with Procter & Gamble in 1895?

options.A: Ada Mayo Stewart
options.B: Clara Barton
options.C: Florence Nightingale
options.D: Alice Hamilton

explanation: Ada Mayo Stewart provided great nursing care to workers and their families, setting an inspiring example for workplace health nurses. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h4)

question: Which specific medication is the go-to emergency antidote for an opioid overdose?

options.A: Vitamin K
options.B: Atropine
options.C: Naloxone
options.D: Digoxin immune fab

explanation: Fantastic! Naloxone quickly blocks opioids and helps the patient breathe normally again. Keep this one locked in your memory! [learn more](GNS221_U3_T14#GNS221_U3_T14_h6)

question: Why must a community health nurse pay special attention to vulnerable groups during an assessment?

options.A: They often lack the voice or resources to access care on their own
options.B: They pay higher taxes to support the local primary health center
options.C: They make up the majority of the staff working in the hospitals
options.D: They are the only people in the community who ever get sick

explanation: Because these groups often suffer quietly without demanding services, it's our duty as nurses to actively find them and be their advocates. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h5)

question: Why does a person's heart beat faster when they have severe anaemia?

options.A: To warm up body tissues chilled by slow blood flow
options.B: To compensate for lower oxygen delivery by pumping blood faster
options.C: To lower high blood pressure from extra red blood cells
options.D: To help the kidneys filter out waste quickly

explanation: Think of it this way: since each drop of blood carries less oxygen, the heart has to pump much faster to make sure vital organs get what they need! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T6#GNS311_U2_T6_h1)

question: A distressed family member is upset because their dying relative refuses to eat meals. What is the most appropriate nursing response?

options.A: Scold the patient for not trying hard enough to maintain their body weight
options.B: Tell the family to force feed the patient large portions using a syringe
options.C: Explain that declining appetite is a natural part of the illness and focus on mouth care
options.D: Insist that the doctor order total parenteral nutrition immediately

explanation: Reassuring the family and shifting attention away from forced feeding reduces anxiety for everyone involved. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T15#GNS321_U4_T15_h5)

question: Where does the hidden majority of sodium in our diets usually come from?

options.A: Hidden additives inside manufactured packaged foods
options.B: Natural spring water consumed throughout the day
options.C: Fresh vegetables grown in mineral-rich soil
options.D: The table salt shaker used right before eating

explanation: Correct! Most of our salt doesn't come from the shaker; it's already tucked away inside processed and packaged foods as a preservative. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T008#GNS227_U6_T008_h4)

question: At what age does a healthy baby usually double their birth weight?

options.A: At 9 months of age
options.B: At 12 months of age
options.C: At 2 months of age
options.D: At 5 months of age

explanation: Great job! A baby typically doubles their birth weight around 5 months and triples it by their first birthday. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T2#GNS225_U3_T2_h2)

question: How does Crohn's disease affect the bowel wall differently from Ulcerative Colitis?

options.A: Crohn's affects the full thickness of the wall, while colitis affects only the mucosa
options.B: Crohn's causes smooth continuous inflammation, while colitis causes patchy skip lesions
options.C: Crohn's affects only the rectum, while colitis affects the small intestine
options.D: Crohn's only causes mild irritation, while colitis always causes complete perforation

explanation: Great job! Crohn's disease goes deep, affecting all layers of the bowel wall (transmural), whereas Ulcerative Colitis stays on the inner lining surface. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h3)

question: As a nurse, how must you make sure the traction weights are positioned during your shift?

options.A: They are adjusted upward by the patient
options.B: They are hidden beneath heavy wool blankets
options.C: They rest securely on the foot of the bed
options.D: They hang freely without touching the floor

explanation: Always check those weights! If they touch the floor, they lose their pulling power and the therapy won't work. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T12#GNS221_U1_T12_h4)

question: What do we call the solid little ball of cells that forms a few days after fertilization?

options.A: Zygote
options.B: Blastocyst
options.C: Morula
options.D: Trophoblast

explanation: You got it! It's called a morula, looking like a tiny, solid cluster of cells before it hollows out into the next stage. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T3#GNS121_U6_T3_h2)

question: What determines the overall size of a non-lactating human breast?

options.A: The amount of adipose tissue
options.B: The length of the milk ducts
options.C: The thickness of the skin
options.D: The number of active lobes

explanation: Fatty, or adipose, tissue makes up the bulk of non-lactating breast size, whereas glandular tissue varies less between individuals. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h3)

question: Why must honey be strictly avoided for infants under one year of age?

options.A: It contains high levels of artificial food coloring
options.B: It always causes immediate childhood obesity
options.C: It carries a severe risk of causing infant botulism
options.D: It replaces the need for essential milk feeds

explanation: Honey can contain spores of the bacterium Clostridium botulinum, which immature infant digestive tracts cannot fight off safely. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h4)

question: Why is sharing login passwords with a colleague considered a serious breach of EHR security?

options.A: It automatically deletes all lab results stored in the database
options.B: It compromises accountability and violates patient confidentiality
options.C: It increases the hospital's monthly internet subscription fee
options.D: It causes the computer screen to freeze and crash completely

explanation: Audit trails link actions to specific user accounts; sharing credentials makes it impossible to know who actually accessed or changed a record. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h7)

question: Oh no! A nurse gets a needle stick injury while dealing with a full sharps box. What is the very first thing she should do?

options.A: Wash the puncture site thoroughly with soap and running water
options.B: Complete an incident report form before washing the wound
options.C: Squeeze the puncture site hard to force out old blood
options.D: Apply a tight tourniquet above the elbow immediately

explanation: You've got it! Immediate washing with soap and running water helps wash away germs right away before you report the incident. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h7)

question: Why are medications like gabapentin or amitriptyline prescribed for some types of chronic pain?

options.A: They act as fast rescue doses for sudden, unexpected pain spikes
options.B: They replace strong opioids so the patient never develops any tolerance
options.C: They are adjuvant drugs that help calm irritated nerves and unusual pain signals
options.D: They cure the underlying tissue damage that caused the discomfort

explanation: Adjuvants are medications developed for other purposes, such as seizures or depression, that prove very effective at treating nerve-related pain. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T14#GNS321_U4_T14_h6)

question: What factor do you look at during a socio-economic and environmental nutritional check?

options.A: Basal energy expenditure measured in a laboratory
options.B: Ability to afford, access, and safely prepare food
options.C: Exact microscopic cellular enzyme activity levels
options.D: Genetic predisposition to inherited metabolic diseases

explanation: Socio-economic checks look at the real-world picture: can they afford food, get to a market, and cook it safely? [learn more](GNS124_U6_T5#GNS124_U6_T5_h5)

question: Why are local leaders and traditional rulers included in primary health care committees?

options.A: They possess formal medical degrees to diagnose patients
options.B: They are responsible for paying health worker salaries
options.C: They help mobilize the community and build trust in health programs
options.D: They supply all the drugs needed for the clinic

explanation: Traditional and community leaders wield great influence, making it easier to convince villagers to accept immunizations and other health interventions. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is the very first thing you put on when wearing a full set of PPE?

options.A: Put on protective eyewear
options.B: Put on the surgical mask
options.C: Put on the isolation gown
options.D: Put on non-sterile gloves

explanation: That's correct! Always start with your gown, tying it securely to cover your uniform first. Your gloves always go on last, right over the gown sleeves. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h3)

question: What is the normal pH range for human arterial blood?
explanation: Keep this number locked in your memory! A pH of 7.35 to 7.45 keeps body enzymes working smoothly and cells happy. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h3)

question: What happens to a regular medication when 'enzyme induction' speeds up its breakdown?

options.A: It blocks the drug from ever entering the gastrointestinal tract
options.B: It raises the blood concentration of the drug to toxic levels instantly
options.C: It lowers the blood concentration of the drug by speeding up its breakdown
options.D: It turns the active drug into a permanent fat-soluble storage molecule

explanation: Induction basically creates a 'night shift' of extra enzymes. They clear out the drug so fast that the medication levels drop below what's needed to help the patient—hello, treatment failure! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T3#GNS125_U5_T3_h6)

question: How do internal audits differ from external audits?

options.A: Internal audits are voluntary suggestions, while external audits are completely illegal
options.B: Internal audits happen once every decade, while external audits happen every morning
options.C: Internal audits are done within the facility, while external ones are done by independent outside bodies
options.D: Internal audits focus only on doctors, while external audits focus only on nurses

explanation: You got it! Internal checks are done by your own hospital team to catch mistakes early, while external checks are done by independent outsiders for an unbiased review. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h5)

question: What are the main hormonal signs that point toward Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)?

options.A: Complete absence of estrogen production
options.B: Permanent closure of the cervical os
options.C: Hyperactivity of the thyroid gland
options.D: Androgen excess and ovulatory dysfunction

explanation: Spot on! PCOS usually brings higher levels of male hormones along with unpredictable or missing ovulation cycles. You are learning clinical concepts like a pro! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h5)

question: How can nurse burnout negatively affect counselling sessions?

options.A: It automatically increases clinic funding
options.B: It reduces the nurse's ability to show empathy
options.C: It removes all language barriers in the room
options.D: It improves the speed of patient discharges

explanation: When you're exhausted and burnt out, it's so much harder to find the emotional energy to deeply connect with your patients. Take care of yourselves, future nurses! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h8)

question: What is the main goal of nutrition counseling given by a nurse?

options.A: To sell government-approved dietary supplements directly from the clinic
options.B: To force the patient to follow a rigid hospital-approved meal plan forever
options.C: To convince the patient that all commercial vitamins are completely toxic
options.D: To guide the patient toward sustainable and balanced eating habits

explanation: Good nursing isn't about temporary fixes; it's about helping patients build healthy eating habits they can actually maintain for life. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T018#GNS227_U2_T018_h7)

question: What is the main job of the motor areas in the brain's cerebral cortex?

options.A: Interpreting sounds and spoken language
options.B: Storing long-term episodic memories
options.C: Controlling voluntary muscle movements
options.D: Processing visual images from the eyes

explanation: You've got this! The motor areas are specially designed to plan and make happen all the voluntary movements your body makes every day. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T10#GNS211_U3_T10_h1)

question: What is a primary nursing responsibility during a routine visit to a day care centre?

options.A: Teaching advanced university nursing courses
options.B: Managing the financial accounts of the facility
options.C: Constructing new playground equipment
options.D: Reviewing child immunization records

explanation: Community health nurses check immunization records to verify that all children are up-to-date on vaccines, protecting the group from outbreaks. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h6)

question: What color zone on a Shakir MUAC tape indicates severe acute malnutrition?

options.A: Green
options.B: Yellow
options.C: Red
options.D: Blue

explanation: The red zone warns of severe malnutrition, signaling that the child needs urgent medical and nutritional rescue. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T9#GNS225_U2_T9_h5)

question: Why is maintaining good hydration especially vital for a bedbound person?

options.A: It replaces the need for physical therapy
options.B: It completely cures physical paralysis over time
options.C: It prevents dehydration that can damage skin integrity
options.D: It stops the patient from feeling hungry

explanation: Adequate fluids keep the skin elastic and well-perfused, reducing the risk of pressure injuries and breakdown. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h4)

question: What is the internationally accepted age below which any marriage is classified as an early or child marriage?

options.A: Under 18 years of age
options.B: Under 15 years of age
options.C: Under 16 years of age
options.D: Under 21 years of age

explanation: Great job! Global health standards consider anyone under 18 a minor. Any union below this age is classed as early marriage, no matter local customs. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T11#GNS312_U1_T11_h1)

question: Why do nurses act as crucial links between affected communities and coordinators?

options.A: They hold the highest administrative rank in disaster management
options.B: They interact directly with victims and understand ground realities
options.C: They are the only health professionals allowed outside hospitals
options.D: They control the transport and logistics budgets for the region

explanation: Because nurses care directly for the victims, they see what resources are missing and report those needs to coordinators. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h4)

question: What is the main way the poliovirus spreads in a community?

options.A: Inhalation of respiratory droplets from sneezing
options.B: Direct skin contact with an infected skin rash
options.C: Vector-borne transmission via mosquito bites
options.D: Fecal-oral route through contaminated water or food

explanation: Spot on! Polio spreads mainly through the fecal-oral route, usually when people consume food or water contaminated with infected waste. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h3)

question: Why do researchers process raw data in nursing studies?

options.A: To hide patient names to protect privacy
options.B: To increase the total number of study participants
options.C: To turn raw information into a structured, usable format
options.D: To write up the final hospital budget report

explanation: Great job thinking about research! Processing simply takes messy field notes or surveys and organizes them so you can actually study what they mean. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T16#GNS217_U3_T16_h1)

question: What is always the very first step in the community health planning cycle?

options.A: Assessment
options.B: Evaluation
options.C: Implementation
options.D: Budgeting

explanation: Spot on! Before you can help or build a program, you first need to assess and understand what is going on in the community. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h2)

question: Who should you talk to first when introducing a new health program to a traditional community?

options.A: Newly graduated nursing students from the city
options.B: Commercial transport drivers in the motor park
options.C: International donor agencies and foreign embassies
options.D: Community leaders and traditional rulers

explanation: You got it! Respecting elders and local leaders opens the door for the community to trust and accept your health program. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T2#GNS214_U1_T2_h5)

question: What does the term "not-invented-here syndrome" mean in a hospital setting?

options.A: Staff reject a new practice simply because they did not come up with it themselves
options.B: Nurses refuse to care for patients admitted from another hospital
options.C: Management bans any new clinical guidelines written by outside experts
options.D: The hospital refuses to buy medical equipment made in foreign countries

explanation: Have you ever seen people reject a good idea just because it wasn't their own? That's 'not-invented-here syndrome'—a common human habit we learn to overcome! [learn more](GST319_U1_T6#GST319_U1_T6_h3)

question: In Nigeria, which level of government is primarily responsible for running Primary Health Care (PHC) centers?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Defence
options.B: Private pharmaceutical companies
options.C: Local Government Council
options.D: International Health Organizations

explanation: Spot on! Primary Health Care in Nigeria is managed closely at the grassroots level by Local Government Councils. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h6)

question: What is a key role of a public health nurse when it comes to sanitation and disease prevention?

options.A: Educating communities about safe water storage and hand hygiene
options.B: Designing and building municipal underground concrete sewer mains
options.C: Operating heavy excavating machinery to fix broken drain fields
options.D: Manufacturing chemical water purification tablets in a laboratory

explanation: As a nurse, your superpower is education! Teaching families about proper handwashing and safe drinking water habits is one of the best ways to stop infections before they start. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h8)

question: A patient falls and cracks the hard outer layer of their thigh bone (femur). Which bone tissue is affected?

options.A: Compact bone
options.B: Cartilaginous bone
options.C: Trabecular bone
options.D: Spongy bone

explanation: Compact bone forms that tough, dense outer shield of long bones. You'll see this often in orthopaedic wards! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T4#GNS121_U3_T4_h3)

question: What does it mean when a drug like phenytoin has a 'narrow therapeutic index'?

options.A: The drug only works on a tiny, specific area of the brain
options.B: Patients must only take the medication once every few weeks
options.C: The drug cannot be absorbed if taken with food in the stomach
options.D: The difference between a safe dose and a toxic dose is very small

explanation: A narrow therapeutic index means we have to walk a tightrope! Too little drug and the seizures return; too much and the patient gets toxic. That's why blood level checks are so crucial. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T3#GNS223_U6_T3_h4)

question: A nurse is getting ready to give a newborn the BCG vaccine. Which technique and site are correct?

options.A: Subcutaneous injection in the fatty abdominal tissue
options.B: Oral drops placed directly onto the infant tongue
options.C: Intramuscular injection in the anterolateral thigh
options.D: Intradermal injection on the upper left arm

explanation: BCG goes right into the upper layer of the skin (intradermally) on the arm, leaving a cute little raised bump! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h4)

question: Why is pulse oximetry sometimes called the fifth vital sign in busy clinical wards?

options.A: It must be recorded before measuring temperature or pulse
options.B: It requires five different fingers to be tested at the same time
options.C: It is checked every five hours on all ward patients
options.D: It provides quick, vital data about oxygenation without invasive blood draws

explanation: Because it gives rapid, essential information about tissue perfusion and oxygenation safely, it ranks alongside standard vital signs. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h1)

question: What dangerous action must nurses warn patients NEVER to do with a maggot-filled skin boil?

options.A: Applying cold compresses to reduce swelling before treatment
options.B: Squeezing or crushing the lesion aggressively with bare hands
options.C: Covering the area loosely with clean cotton gauze
options.D: Washing the surrounding skin gently with clean water and soap

explanation: Squeezing can crush the larva right inside the flesh, triggering a nasty allergic reaction and deep wound infection. Always educate your patients against this! [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h6)

question: A nurse finishes giving an intramuscular injection with a disposable syringe. Where should the nurse discard the needle?

options.A: Inside the general black municipal waste bin
options.B: Into a puncture-resistant yellow safety box
options.C: Inside a regular soft yellow plastic trash bag
options.D: On top of the medication preparation trolley

explanation: Sharps must go directly into a rigid safety box to prevent needle-stick injuries during transport. [learn more](GST114_U2_T14#GST114_U2_T14_h3)

question: What is the difference between a felt need and a real need in community health?

options.A: A felt need is what the community asks for, while a real need is what data shows they lack
options.B: A felt need can be solved with money, while a real need requires federal approval
options.C: A felt need is written in hospital books, while a real need is spoken secretly
options.D: A felt need affects children, while a real need only affects elderly men

explanation: Communities often request things like a big hospital building, when data shows their actual greatest need is clean drinking water to stop cholera. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h5)

question: What is the main job of your eustachian tube when you yawn or swallow on a flight?

options.A: To amplify high-frequency sound waves
options.B: To translate fluid waves into nerve impulses
options.C: To equalize air pressure in the middle ear
options.D: To produce earwax for protection

explanation: That "pop" you feel in your ears when swallowing helps the eustachian tube let air in or out, keeping the pressure balanced on both sides of your eardrum. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T7#GNS211_U4_T7_h3)

question: What is a key time-based rule for diagnosing obsessive-compulsive neurosis?

options.A: Behaviors must last continuously for at least five full years
options.B: The episodes must happen only once every month without fail
options.C: The rituals must occur strictly during morning hours upon waking
options.D: Symptoms must take up more than one hour daily or cause marked distress

explanation: Correct! For a formal diagnosis, these thoughts or rituals usually need to steal over an hour of the patient's day or cause serious distress. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T7#GNS314_U2_T7_h4)

question: How does a standard pacemaker actually assist the heart muscle?

options.A: By sending tiny electrical pulses to prompt regular contractions
options.B: By pumping blood directly through plastic tubes into the aorta
options.C: By delivering high-energy shocks to restart a stopped heart
options.D: By permanently replacing the heart valves with mechanical gates

explanation: The device acts as an artificial electrical conductor, firing small pulses to make the heart muscle contract at a safe rate. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h1)

question: What is the special thing about a "community of solution"?

options.A: Its members interact exclusively through mobile phone apps
options.B: It forms around a specific problem or shared health goal
options.C: It exists permanently within a single government district
options.D: It is defined strictly by natural rivers and mountains

explanation: Nice one! These groups team up specifically to tackle and solve a particular issue or health challenge together. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T2#GNS225_U1_T2_h3)

question: A young adult is admitted after taking too many sleeping pills on purpose. They are now fully awake and stable. What is your most important immediate nursing action?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately with a prescription for vitamins.
options.B: Initiate strict suicide precautions and ensure constant observation.
options.C: Scold the patient regarding the dangers of taking medication.
options.D: Restrict all family members from visiting to maintain hospital quiet.

explanation: Just because they look physically stable doesn't mean the emotional crisis is over. Safety first—keep them under close watch and arrange mental health support right away. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of a home visit in community nursing?

options.A: To perform major surgical procedures at home
options.B: To assess the financial status of the family
options.C: To provide care in the patient's natural environment
options.D: To replace hospital admission completely

explanation: Home visits bring healthcare directly to where patients live so nurses can see their everyday environment and support them there. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h1)

question: A 14-year-old girl who has recently started menstruating is at a higher risk for running low on which nutrient?

options.A: Sodium
options.B: Iron
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Potassium

explanation: You got it! Monthly period blood loss combined with rapid body growth means she needs extra iron to keep her energy up and prevent anemia. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h2)

question: Why is adequate iron intake particularly crucial immediately following childbirth and during lactation?

options.A: To help the infant digest complex carbohydrates in the milk
options.B: To stimulate the mammary glands to produce more milk volume
options.C: To prevent postpartum anemia and recover from blood loss during delivery
options.D: To regulate the mother's blood pressure during night feeds

explanation: Childbirth involves blood loss, and iron helps build new red blood cells to keep the mother strong and energized. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h4)

question: Which communication channel works best when discussing sensitive personal health issues?

options.A: A large billboard placed on the highway
options.B: Interpersonal communication like counseling
options.C: An anonymous pamphlet dropped in the mail
options.D: A commercial broadcast on national television

explanation: Face-to-face counseling builds trust and allows for private, two-way chats. It's the gold standard for sensitive topics! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T7#GNS124_U5_T7_h5)

question: What is the best way to report a patient's death when calling the doctor?

options.A: Provide a concise report of assessment findings and absent vital signs
options.B: Wait until the morning shift change before making the phone call
options.C: Ask the physician for permission to start post-mortem care immediately
options.D: Ask the doctor to sign the death certificate over the telephone

explanation: Well done! Giving quick, clear facts helps the doctor understand what's happening before they even step into the room. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T9#GNS221_U4_T9_h5)

question: A clinic notices that the cash counted at day's end is less than the value of drugs sold. What should management do first?

options.A: Stop ordering new medications until patient attendance increases
options.B: Conduct a thorough audit of daily sales records and collection points
options.C: Transfer all pharmacy staff to different departments in the hospital
options.D: Increase the selling price of all essential medicines immediately

explanation: Good clinical management means investigating before accusing! An audit helps you find where money is leaking—whether through errors or missing cash. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T3#GNS215_U3_T3_h2)

question: What is 'diagnostic overshadowing' in clinical practice?

question: Which protective gear is a must-have when working near an active X-ray machine?

question: What is a major barrier that stops eligible people from using public food support systems?

question: Who among the following is NOT usually in the high-risk group for severe food poisoning?

question: Why should nursing educators pay attention to environmental factors?

question: Why does a subcutaneous injection take longer to work than an IV injection?

question: Why do nurses need to look beyond the hospital walls when caring for patients?

options.A: Clinical treatments alone are completely useless without government approval
options.B: Patients expect nurses to solve their personal family conflicts

question: Which statistical test should you use to compare the average scores of two completely separate groups of patients?

question: How does a literature review directly help with everyday bedside nursing care?

question: Which of these is NOT a typical duty of a community health nurse in disease control?

question: How does regular physical exercise help lower a person's blood sugar?

question: What is the purpose of comparing local community health statistics with national standards?

question: Why should you ask a patient about their alcohol intake when doing a blood assessment?

question: A patient worries that a missing fallopian tube means she can never have a family. What is the best initial nursing response?

question: What is the main difference between a reservoir and a source of infection?

question: What are Cheyne-Stokes respirations?

question: Why should nurses care about why patients stay silent when safety rules are skipped?

question: Which nursing action is most important when putting in a urinary catheter?

question: Which model of adult day care focuses primarily on meals, recreation, and socialization without intensive health services?

question: Which of these is NOT a safe or recommended way to lower your risk of getting an STI?

question: A sudden plant disease wipes out a large portion of local cassava crops. Based on market dynamics, what is the most likely immediate result for consumers?

question: What is the main reason a bag of blood must be completely infused within four hours?

question: Where does fertilization of the egg by the sperm normally take place in the female reproductive tract?

question: A nurse finishes emptying a utility bin filled with used dressings and removes her heavy utility gloves. What is the immediate next step she should take?

question: What should be included in a good community action plan?

question: In SOAP charting, what kind of details go into the 'O' (Objective) section?

question: What three factors make up 'Virchow's triad' for blood clot formation?

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of an allergic reaction after administering eye drops?

question: How does knowing basic biographical data like a patient's age and gender help during a bone and joint assessment?

question: What is the primary goal of health education in schools?

question: Why is Vitamin K so effective at reversing the effects of warfarin?

question: What should a unit manager do when staff members have a workplace conflict?

question: At what exact moment during patient care should you sort and throw away your waste?

question: How does it affect disaster response when agencies work in isolated 'silos'?

question: What is a major benefit of using an epidural for pain relief during labor for a patient with sickle cell disease?

question: Why do quality improvement projects usually start on a small scale instead of rolling out hospital-wide?

options.C: Direct government orders prohibiting doctors from asking about it
options.D: A complete absence of physical symptoms requiring medical care

explanation: Because family members enforce strict silence, victims rarely speak out due to intimidation and cultural norms. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T17#GNS312_U1_T17_h2)

question: A patient has a hard mass of stool stuck in the rectum (impaction), yet they keep passing small amounts of liquid. Why does this happen?

options.A: Infection has completely liquefied the entire colon
options.B: Liquid stool leaks around the solid blocked mass
options.C: The small intestine is hyperactive and rushing food
options.D: The kidneys are producing excessive fluid waste

explanation: Don't let this trick you in the ward! Liquid waste from higher up in the gut finds a way to slip past the hard, blocked stool, which can easily look like normal diarrhea. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h1)

question: What is the main sign that a mum is experiencing distress during labour?

options.A: Complete absence of uterine contractions
options.B: A sudden drop in maternal blood pressure
options.C: An increase in fetal heart rate baseline
options.D: Severe physical and emotional exhaustion

explanation: Maternal distress happens when the physical and emotional weight of labour completely overwhelms the mum's coping powers. Spotting this early lets you step in with a comforting touch! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T002#GNS226_U4_T002_h1)

question: What does the lab usually do if the name on a specimen tube doesn't match the request form?

options.A: Fix the typo themselves without informing the ward
options.B: Reject the specimen and request a new collection
options.C: Call the doctor to guess which patient it belongs to
options.D: Process the sample anyway using the bed number

explanation: Labs have zero tolerance for mismatched names because it's a huge safety hazard. They will throw it out and ask for a fresh sample. [learn more](GST114_U5_T1#GST114_U5_T1_h6)

question: What should you do right away if you evaluate your patient and see they haven't met their care goal?

options.A: Wait until the next morning doctor's rounds to report it
options.B: Discontinue all monitoring devices to reduce patient stress
options.C: Reassess the patient and modify the plan of care
options.D: Document that the patient is impossible to treat

explanation: Don't panic if a goal isn't met—that's totally normal nursing! It just means it's time to cycle back, figure out what's going on, and tweak your game plan. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T8#GNS321_U2_T8_h6)

question: A patient comes in with right upper quadrant belly pain, fever, and a history of dysentery. What condition should you suspect?

options.A: A perforated stomach ulcer
options.B: An amoebic liver abscess
options.C: Acute appendicitis
options.D: Severe kidney stones

explanation: Spot on! When the parasites travel up into the liver via the bloodstream, they can form a painful, pus-filled abscess. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h3)

question: What important task must a nurse do right after a surgical uterine evacuation?

options.A: Perform a pelvic exam without gloves
options.B: Discharge the patient home right away
options.C: Administer general anesthesia
options.D: Inspect the removed tissue to confirm everything came out

explanation: Always check the evacuated tissue! It guarantees no tissue was left behind, keeping the patient safe from infection. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h5)

question: Why does the ventral respiratory group kick in when someone starts exercising hard?

options.A: To slow down the breathing rate and conserve energy
options.B: To drive forceful exhalation and deeper breaths required by the exertion
options.C: To bypass the damaged pons and restore normal speech
options.D: To cool down the brainstem through rapid airflow

explanation: Quiet breathing is mostly about inhaling, but heavy exercise requires extra effort. That's when the ventral group steps in to help you breathe out forcefully. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T14#GNS211_U3_T14_h4)

question: Which of these is a dangerous mistake during an emergency obstetric triage?

options.A: Notifying the medical doctor immediately upon finding abnormal bleeding
options.B: Placing an unstable patient in a quiet resuscitation bay
options.C: Delaying vital sign assessment to fill out admission paperwork
options.D: Checking maternal blood pressure upon entry

explanation: Never let paperwork delay patient care! In emergencies, checking vital signs and stabilizing the patient comes first. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h5)

question: A patient is having trouble controlling their body temperature and fluid balance. Which brain structure is likely involved?

options.A: Occipital lobe
options.B: Broca's area
options.C: Cerebellum
options.D: Hypothalamus

explanation: The hypothalamus is like your body's internal thermostat and control center for thirst, hunger, and temperature. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h4)

question: Which special cells in the stomach lining make hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor?

options.A: Chief cells
options.B: Parietal cells
options.C: Goblet cells
options.D: Mucus neck cells

explanation: Parietal cells are the acid-makers of the stomach, and they also produce intrinsic factor which helps your body absorb vitamin B12. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T3#GNS121_U1_T3_h3)

question: Why is the nursing process so helpful when caring for patients with blood disorders?

options.A: It stops patients from ever developing secondary hospital infections
options.B: It completely replaces the need for routine physician medical orders
options.C: It offers a systematic framework to manage complex and systemic pathologies
options.D: It guarantees that laboratory values will return to normal overnight

explanation: Because blood flows everywhere, a blood disorder affects the whole body. Using the nursing process helps you stay organized and keep your patient safe step-by-step! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h1)

question: What is the main goal of health insurance schemes like the NHIA?

options.A: To provide free international travel for senior nurses
options.B: To guarantee large profits for private insurance companies
options.C: To eliminate the need for doctors in primary health centers
options.D: To pool financial risks and reduce out-of-pocket spending

explanation: Insurance pools everyone's contributions together so that when someone falls sick, they don't have to pay massive cash on the spot. [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h8)
